channel.title: Local News Wire Broadcast Feed
channel.description: Approved local stories in broadcast order

item.description: A coastal storm brought freezing rain and strong winds to Vermont and northern New York last night. Wind gusts reached up to sixty miles per hour in Rutland and Bennington counties. Power outages and hazardous travel conditions were reported. Green Mountain Power, Vermont Electric Cooperative, Town of Stowe and Washington Electric Co-op report three thousand sixty five customers still without power in Vermont this morning.

The Regional Food Bank gave out over five hundred seventy thousand meals across New York this Thanksgiving. In the North Country, about ten thousand meals were distributed at several locations including Plattsburgh and Ticonderoga. Volunteers helped provide free Thanksgiving meals to thousands in need.

The Holiday Train stopped in Port Henry on Thanksgiving to collect donations for local shelters. Free concerts were held to encourage giving. The train has raised over twenty-eight million dollars and five million pounds of food since it began.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul delayed Medicaid work requirements until June next year. The rules require recipients to show eighty hours a month of work or education, with some exemptions. The state is upgrading systems and hopes for federal changes to ease these rules.
